messages:
oliver: Quick heads up — I see an 8-12% tail-latency regression on 8k sequences after today's kernel-selection tweak (commit 4f2a3b). Perf tests on dedicated-staging.

nidhi: yup saw it on canary too. 95p went from 210ms -> 235ms on p4d.

sam: which trace? nsys or perfetto?

oliver: nsys + perfetto. here's the nsys command I ran:
```
nsys profile --output=after_4f2a3b --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite --duration 30s ./bench_runner --seq_len=8192 --batch=1
```

oliver: quick nsys hotspot (simplified):
```
matmul_opt_kernel    45ms -> 70ms
gemm_plain_kernel    60ms -> 80ms (more launches)
kernel_launch_overhead increased ~2x
```

jess: interesting — I also saw KV cache miss-rate bump for same traces, maybe due to different batching order. kv_hit_rate 98.7% -> 96.1% in perf logs.

perf-bot: perf test summary: commit 4f2a3b: +9.4% 95p latency on long seq; commit reverted (4f2a3b~1) back to baseline.

sam: ran git bisect, seems to land on 4f2a3b. patch changed kernel chooser from `score = latency_est + jitter_penalty` to `score = latency_est * stability_pref`.

nidhi: perfetto timeline comparison: when stable-pref is on we prefer matmul_opt for short seq but it underperforms for long seq because it doesn't reuse cached kernels -> more kernel loads. link: https://perfetto.example.com/compare/4f2a3b_vs_prev

oliver: logs showing increased kernel loads per request:
```
[2026-03-16T12:13:34Z] kernel_load_count: 4 -> 9
[2026-03-16T12:13:34Z] kv_cache_evictions: 0.2% -> 2.8%
```

jess: can we add a guard: if seq_len >= 4096 prefer kernels with lower launch overhead even if slightly higher single-op latency? quick experiment patch below.

jess: patch:
```
// prefer low-launch-overhead kernels for long sequences
if (seq_len >= 4096) score += launch_overhead_weight * launch_overhead;
```

sam: tried that locally, 95p back within 1% of baseline. run full perf on staging now.

ci-bot: scheduled e2e-perf job on dedicated-staging for commit jess/guard-4k (run #458)

nidhi: leaving notes for rollout: 1) add opt-in flag for heuristic, 2) add synthetic trace test for kernel-load count, 3) add kv-cache warmup test in nightly.

oliver: thanks. assigning follow-ups: @jess open PR with tests, @sam monitor e2e results, I'll prepare rollback in case.

jess: on it. :thumbsup:
